original_registry_entry.issuing_organisation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
original_registry_entry.version: NICE clinical guideline CG111, published 2010 and last reviewed 2018
original_registry_entry.jurisdiction: England, United Kingdom; international guidance requiring UAE adaptation
original_registry_entry.population: Children and young people under 19 with bedwetting.
original_registry_entry.clinical_setting: Primary, community and specialist assessment and management of bedwetting.
original_registry_entry.applicability_note: Exact for documenting bedwetting pattern, daytime urinary symptoms, fluid and toileting history, relevant comorbidity, examination or investigation context, information, referral and follow-up discussion. It does not diagnose, prescribe or generate referral automatically.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.1–1.3.20 — assessment and investigation
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting onset, prior dryness, bedwetting pattern, daytime urinary symptoms, toileting and fluid intake, comorbidities, clinically selected urinalysis or referral context, and findings from history without autonomous diagnosis.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.2.1–1.2.3 and 1.4.1–1.4.2 — information and management planning
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports recording information given, family priorities, support needs and clinician-entered management or follow-up discussion without selecting treatment.

exact_sections.heading: Recommendations 1.3.10–1.3.15 and 1.8–1.9 — referral, response and recurrence
exact_sections.evidence_summary: Supports documenting severe daytime symptoms, recurrent infection, suspected physical or neurological problems, referral or review and recurrence context without automated escalation.

jurisdiction: England, United Kingdom; international guidance requiring UAE adaptation
